items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: In 1914 and 1915, I was with Giordina. The reason I like Giordina's band is because, first of all, he could be independent.

ctx.x: When you first started beating drums, how old were you?

Well, I was playing in 1912, actually, making a dollar. In 1913, I got a little better. In 1914 and 1915, I was with Giordina. The reason I like Giordina's band is because, first of all, he could be independent. He had a good job, and he picked all good men that could teach me something. You understand? You play with a bad band, you're a young man to learn. Every man in his band was qualified. In fact, even these bands are today. Any of them down the street wouldn't play the rags that Giordina played that time. I…
They can't cut those standard high-class rags?

items.title: Tony Parenti and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-06-29
items.q: In a short while, Edwards started writing to me. For this reason, I had been playing with Giordina, with Edwards.

ctx.x: And all the white people that really opened their door and enjoyed themselves, paid a little amount, whatever it was. It wasn't much money. You know, people can't just... But there was never no dissension. No. Never none of that stuff. That's the ridiculous thing, that dissension for... My gosh, I can never... Well, take for instance, those boys just go out there and catch catfish. Catfish is the big type of fish that is the best fried fish. In fact, I still think catfish... You ought to know, because you're one…

play the bass with you, I'll go buy one on time. I said okay I'll take you over to the World Line Music Store and I did. We got a big sousaphone for him and he brought it down to his job. He had it in traction high, he had it hung up so that all he had to do was get into this big part of it. A bell. And he'd stand up and play. And he played with him. And he was a member of that little band of mine for many, for the entire length of time at the La Vida, which from there his reputation became known and they became…
Henry. I want to get that straight. There's so many out.
